scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

F-01.statement: Field route completion was 0.88 against a 0.95 target for 9200 manual-read accounts over period 2026-08..09.

F-02.statement: Disputed bills by read type: 1240 with read_type ESTIMATED, 1785 with read_type ACTUAL.

F-03.statement: Dispute ticket response times: median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, against a 3.0-day SLA, across 2440 tickets.

F-04.statement: Billing-db tariff change log returned 0 records for the queried period, indicating no recorded tariff rate changes.

F-05.statement: Dispute volume by month: 610 (2026-06), 590 (2026-07), 1180 (2026-08), 1260 (2026-09), roughly doubling from Jun-Jul to Aug-Sep.

F-06.statement: Service contract §4.2 permits the utility to request route priority changes, but execution occurs only after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

F-07.statement: route-log lagging_routes query returned 14 routes with completion values below schedule, sample record: route R-00 at 0.70 completion.

F-08.statement: mdms-export read_events_for_disputed_estimated returned 2 records: 1184 AMI reads received before cutoff and exported_to_billing=true but billing_import_status=REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION; 56 reads with ami_read_before_cutoff=false, billing_import_status=NO_READ_RECEIVED, exported_to_billing=false.

F-09.statement: billing-config validation_rule_changes log shows rule BV-17 (high-consumption check: raw register value vs 12-month m3 history, unit_scaling: none) deployed 2026-08-01, and rule BV-09 (label text change) deployed 2026-03-02.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-RESPONSE-SPEED-FRAMING.statement: Dispute volume doubled mainly because ticket response/resolution capacity is inadequate, so an AI auto-answer agent would resolve the surge.

H-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules introduced around August caused systematic bill errors that drove the dispute surge.

H-AMI-DATA-FAILURE.statement: AMI read delivery or validation failures from the vendor-run MDMS produced missing/bad interval reads, forcing estimate billing and causing wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE.statement: Manual field meter read quality or completion dropped, increasing estimate substitution and producing inaccurate bills.

H-ESTIMATE-LOGIC-DEFECT.statement: The billing system's own estimate-substitution logic, used when no accepted read exists, is generating incorrect bills independent of upstream read quality.

H-ACTUAL-READ-BILLING-DEFECT.statement: A billing-calculation defect (e.g., tariff application or import validation) is producing wrong bills even on correctly-captured ACTUAL meter reads, independent of read-source quality.

H-IMPORT-REJECTS-HIGH-CONSUMPT.statement: Billing import validation rejects legitimately-captured AMI reads flagged as high-consumption (billing_import_status=REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) even when exported before cutoff, forcing estimate substitution for 1184/1240 of the disputed-ESTIMATED subset.

H-BV17-UNIT-SCALING-DEFECT.statement: Rule BV-17 compares raw cumulative register values against 12-month m3 consumption history without applying unit/scale normalization (unit_scaling: none), causing legitimately high but valid consumption readings to be mis-flagged and rejected at import.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Field route completion log shows manual-read route completion ran at 0.88 against a 0.95 target for 9200 manual-read accounts over Aug-Sep 2026, indicating a shortfall in manual meter-read coverage during the dispute-surge period.

Observation still shows manual-read route completion at 0.88 against a 0.95 target for 9200 accounts over Aug-Sep 2026 (a real field operations gap). It no longer supports that this completion shortfall materially drives estimate substitution in the disputed subset: E-11 shows 1184/1240 (95.5%) of those ESTIMATED-dispute accounts actually had a valid pre-cutoff AMI read that was rejected at billing import, not a missing read from a lagging route; only 56 cases show a genuine no-read condition.

Of disputed bills, 1785 involved ACTUAL (meter-captured) reads versus 1240 involving ESTIMATED reads, so a majority (59%) of disputes occur on bills where a read was actually obtained, not just estimate-substituted bills.

Observation still shows 1240 disputed bills with read_type ESTIMATED versus 1785 with read_type ACTUAL. It no longer supports treating ESTIMATED-read and ACTUAL-read disputes as two distinct causal populations (field/estimate-driven versus billing-driven): E-11 shows 1184 of the 1240 ESTIMATED-subset accounts also trace to the same billing-import REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION mechanism, so one dominant billing-import defect, not read-source quality, likely explains the bulk of both subsets.

CRM data shows dispute ticket response times (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days) are already within the 3.0-day SLA across 2440 tickets, so slow response handling is not an observed bottleneck for the ticket surge.

Billing-db's tariff change log returned zero records, meaning no tariff rate changes are on record for the queried period, so a tariff-rate change cannot be the mechanism behind wrong bills on correctly-captured ACTUAL reads.

E-05.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) states no tariff change occurred this year. This stakeholder claim is non-authoritative but agrees in direction with the tool-sourced tariff_change_log (E-04), which already found zero recorded tariff changes; it adds no new evidence toward diagnosing the billing defect.

E-06.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD claims a reader staffing shortfall of three since July causes routes to run late, with affected customers receiving estimated bills instead of manual reads. This is an unverified stakeholder explanation for part of the estimate-substitution path already quantified in E-01, offered by a stakeholder whose incentive is a contract headcount increase and who is flagged as biased toward staffing attribution.

CRM dispute_volume_monthly shows ticket counts of 610 (Jun-26), 590 (Jul-26), 1180 (Aug-26), 1260 (Sep-26): volume roughly doubled from the Jun-Jul baseline (~600/month) to Aug-Sep (~1180-1260/month), confirming the surge's timing and magnitude but saying nothing about its cause.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Service contract §4.2 (document review) confirms the utility may request route priority changes but execution requires Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD) confirmation, consistent with the existing K-DISPATCH authority constraint. This detail concerns the push_route_update protected action's authorization mechanism and bears no causal relevance to the billing dispute surge's root cause.

E-09.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log.lagging_routes returns 14 specific routes with per-route completion values (sample: R-00 at 0.70), giving route-level granularity under the aggregate 0.88/0.95 completion shortfall already in E-01. It identifies which routes are behind but says nothing about why (staffing vs. another cause), so it does not resolve the causal question behind U-FIELD-SHORTFALL-CAUSE/VOB-R-2.

E-10.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI (non-authoritative stakeholder message) claims MDMS export access for Lakeside is now provisioned per vendor ticket TX-4471; this is an unverified claim about access status, not a tool-confirmed read of AMI data, and it does not itself speak to whether AMI read failures contributed to the dispute surge (that question is already settled against by E-02).

A direct AMI read-event query for the disputed-ESTIMATED accounts (totaling exactly 1240, matching E-02) shows 1184 reads were received before cutoff and exported to billing but rejected by billing import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, while only 56 show a genuine missing-read (NO_READ_RECEIVED) case; this identifies billing-import rejection of valid high-consumption reads, not AMI/field read failure, as the mechanism forcing estimate substitution in the vast majority of this subset.

E-12.content: billing-config.validation_rule_changes → 2 record(s): {"change": "high-consumption check compares raw register value with 12-month m3 history", "deployed": "2026-08-01", "rule": "BV-17", "unit_scaling": "none"}; {"change": "label text", "deployed": "2026-03-02", "rule": "BV-09"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-config's validation_rule_changes log shows rule BV-17, deployed exactly 2026-08-01, changed the high-consumption check to compare the raw register value against 12-month m3 history with no unit scaling applied; the only other recent change (BV-09, 2026-03-02) was a cosmetic label edit unrelated to validation logic. BV-17's deployment date lines up precisely with the Aug-Sep dispute surge onset (E-07) and offers a concrete mechanism (unscaled raw-register-vs-m3-history comparison) that plausibly produces the REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION outcome already observed in E-11.

U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMATION.question: Did billing import validation rules actually change around August 2026, and what specifically changed, per the billing-config rule change log (DA-RULES)?
U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMATION.decision_impact: The root-cause mechanism (H-RULE-CHANGE) and any bill-correction candidate work depend on direct confirmation from DA-RULES rather than elimination alone.
U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMATION.resolution_path: Query billing-config rule_change_log and correlate the change date with the dispute_volume_monthly surge onset (E-07).
U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMATION.safe_placeholder: Proceed with diagnostic investigation only; do not generate bill-correction candidates until the rule change is confirmed.
U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMATION.resolution: Confirmed: billing-config's rule change log shows BV-17, a high-consumption check comparing raw register value to 12-month m3 history with no unit scaling, deployed 2026-08-01 - matching the Aug dispute-surge onset (E-07); no other substantive validation rule change occurred in the period (E-12).

U-AMI-ACCESS-PENDING.question: Can AMI read event data be obtained from the vendor-run MDMS (mdms-export) to assess AMI-side contribution to the ESTIMATED-read dispute subset, given the tool is DEGRADED and vendor access is ACCESS_PENDING?
U-AMI-ACCESS-PENDING.decision_impact: Without AMI interval data, the AMI contribution to the minority ESTIMATED-read dispute subset remains unconfirmed, though it does not affect the dominant ACTUAL-read mechanism.
U-AMI-ACCESS-PENDING.resolution_path: Await vendor provisioning of mdms-export access; retry read_events_for_disputed_estimated once ACCESS_PENDING clears.
U-AMI-ACCESS-PENDING.safe_placeholder: Rely on the current ACTUAL vs ESTIMATED split (E-02) and treat AMI-side contribution to the ESTIMATED subset as unconfirmed in the interim.
U-AMI-ACCESS-PENDING.resolution: mdms-export returned a COMPLETE, AUTHORITATIVE read of event data for the disputed-ESTIMATED subset (E-11), confirming vendor-provisioned access is now usable and closing the access-pending question.

U-FIELD-SHORTFALL-CAUSE.question: Is the field route completion shortfall (0.88 vs 0.95 target, E-01) actually caused by the reader staffing shortage SH-FIELD claims (E-06), or by another cause, given SH-FIELD has an incentive toward a contract headcount increase?
U-FIELD-SHORTFALL-CAUSE.decision_impact: Determines whether push_route_update (route reprioritization) is the correct secondary mitigation or whether a different field-process fix is needed.
U-FIELD-SHORTFALL-CAUSE.resolution_path: Audit field dispatch assignment and completion records independently of SH-FIELD's self-report before acting on route changes.
U-FIELD-SHORTFALL-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: Treat push_route_update as a candidate mitigation only, pending independent confirmation of the shortfall's cause.

U-DATA-COMPLETENESS.question: Are the billing, route and rule-change data assets (DA-BILL, DA-ROUTE, DA-RULES) complete enough to support a definitive root-cause conclusion, given their completeness is marked UNKNOWN?
U-DATA-COMPLETENESS.decision_impact: Incomplete source data could change the 59%/41% ACTUAL/ESTIMATED split and the strength of the rule-change inference.
U-DATA-COMPLETENESS.resolution_path: Check completeness flags on DA-BILL, DA-ROUTE and DA-RULES before finalizing the root-cause conclusion.
U-DATA-COMPLETENESS.safe_placeholder: Treat the current read-type split and rule-change hypothesis as provisional pending completeness confirmation.

U-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.question: Are the H-FIELD-BILL (manual read upload) and H-MDMS-BILL (AMI export) handoffs into billing delivering complete, semantically valid read data, given both show delivery_status and semantic_validity as UNKNOWN?
U-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.decision_impact: If reads delivered via these handoffs are incomplete or invalid, the read-type split underlying H-RULE-CHANGE (E-02) and any bill-correction candidate list could be unreliable.
U-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Validate H-FIELD-BILL and H-MDMS-BILL delivery_status and semantic_validity against source system logs before relying on billing-db read-type counts.
U-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Treat the current ACTUAL/ESTIMATED split (E-02) as provisional; do not finalize bill-correction candidates until handoff validity is confirmed.
U-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.resolution: For 1184/1240 disputed-ESTIMATED accounts, E-11 shows exported_to_billing=true (H-MDMS-BILL handoff delivered valid data); the rejection occurs downstream at billing import validation, not at the handoff; 56/1240 show genuine non-delivery (NO_READ_RECEIVED, exported_to_billing=false), partially resolving the H-MDMS-BILL side of this unknown.
